judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short insuring promise to pay proceeds 'according to the following provisions'; the operative words are generic and heavily OCR-degraded but carry no genuinely competing meaning on their face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defers wholly to Sections 4 and 5, and I found no operative provision it contradicts, though it is the hook by which any proceeds dispute (4.1, 5.10) is framed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard free-look language; 'within 20 days after you receive it' is a definite period, and the garbling is transcription rather than drafting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in Section 3 (premium payment) or 7.2 (effective date) contradicts a refund on return within 20 days.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Paid-up for level life insurance' with a death benefit 'level amount based on the current Policy Account Value less any Policy Indebtedness' is incomplete and its measure of benefit is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits awkwardly against Section 4.2's Coverage Option A/B death-benefit formulas and the Specified Amount, since after age 95 the benefit would apparently be account-value based rather than the Specified Amount.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definitional preamble stating that Sections 3-10 give a 'more complete description'; it creates no operative right and names no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It functions as an interpretive priority rule subordinating Section 2 definitions to later sections, which could matter if a definition (e.g. 2.15's cross-reference) conflicts with the operative text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple identification of the Insured as the person whose death causes proceeds to be paid; no competing reading.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.1 and Section 1's designation of Ms. Antonio as both Owner and Insured.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definition of 'you' as the Owner, expressly allowing Owner and Insured to differ; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits Section 8.1-8.2 on ownership and change of ownership without tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure party identification of the insurer; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision uses 'we' differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Truncated definition ('as named in the original application but may subsequently be changed'); the change mechanism is not stated here, but the term itself is not ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends entirely on Section 8.4, which adds that the Owner is beneficiary if none is named — a gap in 2.4 rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The total amount we are obligated to pay' on death or on surrender; the phrase 'while this Policy is in force and the Insured is alive' is oddly placed but the sense is recoverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Squares with 4.1 (Surrender Value if living, Death Proceeds if not) and 5.7; I found no clause defining Proceeds differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite computational anchor date shown in Section 1; nothing vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently by 2.17 (Monthly Due Date) and 7.2 (Effective Date); the Section 1 specifications page is largely illegible, which is an evidentiary rather than construction problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The date coverage commences' is a one-line definition that simply cross-refers elsewhere; little to construe in itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It points to Section 7.2 for the initial policy, while 3.1 says there is 'no insurance coverage in effect until the payment is made' — three provisions on when coverage starts that must be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A stranded fragment ('age on the birthday nearest the first...'); as written it does not state a complete rule, though the standard nearest-birthday convention is recoverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Age drives the 5.4 cost-of-insurance table and the 4.2 corridor percentages, so an incomplete age definition could unsettle both.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Planned Periodic Premium ... is the minimum that must be paid' during the first two years sits beside the statement that payments may exceed the amount 'required at any time'; what is 'required' is not clearly fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with 3.2(1)-(2) and the 5.10 no-lapse test, which measure the first-two-year obligation differently (a running one-twelfth-per-month test rather than a flat minimum).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-sentence definition tying the Minimum Initial Premium to a Section 1 figure; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.1 and 7.2, both of which condition coverage on its payment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Badly truncated ('the amount you specified in the original application ... used in determining the amount of death benefit'), but the concept is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.2 supplies the increase/decrease mechanism it cross-refers to; no contradiction located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definition of Death Benefit 'prior to any adjustment specified in Section 4'; the reference to unspecified adjustments is broad but Section 4 supplies them.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.2 both computes and then adjusts (riders up, indebtedness down), so the definition and operative text can be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'An increased death benefit when the difference between the Policy Account Value and the death benefit reaches a minimum size' uses the undefined and vague phrase 'minimum size'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The corridor is actually implemented by the age-percentage table in 4.2, so the definition's vague formulation is cured only by reading the later section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is clear in substance but closes with 'See Section 4.3', a mis-citation: the Monthly Insurance Charge is Section 5.3 and 4.3 is interest on death proceeds.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That wrong cross-reference is a defect in the provision's relationship to Sections 4.3 and 5.3, though the correct target is obvious enough to be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The charge we make for providing pure insurance protection using the current Cost of Insurance rates' is definite in form, though 'current' rates are set by the insurer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cross-reference to 5.4 is correct and 5.4 supplies the formula and guaranteed maximums; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The same day of each month as shown in the Policy Date' is a mechanical rule with no competing reading.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used identically in 5.3, 5.10 and 9.2; consistent throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'There is no insurance coverage in effect until the payment is made' is an absolute statement whose interaction with delivery timing is not spelled out here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pulls against 7.2, which makes the policy effective on the later of the Policy Date or payment and refers to a Temporary Insurance Agreement given when the premium was taken — a genuine tension over pre-delivery coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'You may make premium payments at any time and in any amount you choose subject to the following' is a general grant expressly qualified by an enumerated list, the classic general-versus-specific posture.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The four numbered limits and 3.3's tax cap all cut back the general freedom, so its real scope is only knowable from the rest of Section 3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text has dropped its middle ('the total of your premium payments during the first two policy years must be at least the Planned Periodic Premium'), leaving an incomplete sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with 3.2(2) and 5.10's no-lapse test, which state the first-two-year requirement on a monthly pro-rata basis rather than as a lump minimum.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed but arithmetically explicit rule (one-twelfth of annual Planned Periodic Premium times elapsed months); precise rather than vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the no-lapse formula in 5.10 almost word for word, which supports rather than undermines coherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite floor on remittances with a unilateral right to change it on notice; the discretion is broad but the words are not ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.9's reference to the Minimum Premium Remittance shown in Section 1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'We may establish minimum and maximum limitations' followed by 'This will happen only if payment ... would increase the difference between the death benefit and the Policy Account Value' is a confusingly drafted condition whose trigger is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with the 4.2 corridor (which itself widens the gap automatically) and with 3.3's tax limit, leaving the insurer's power to refuse premiums stated in two different places on different tests.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The tax citations are garbled and open-ended ('or any future applicable regulations'), but the operative right — refuse or return excess premium — is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with 3.2(4)'s separate power to limit additional premiums; two premium-refusal powers on different triggers, which is duplicative rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'May be reinstated within five years after the expiration of the Grace Period and prior to the surrender of the Policy' is legible, but the OCR scrambling leaves the trigger sentence incomplete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reinstatement presupposes the lapse mechanics of 5.10 and the separate lapse trigger in 9.4, and this is the kind of clause a lapse dispute turns on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line fragment requiring 'evidence of insurability'; that phrase is a familiar term of art but is left unqualified here (satisfactory to whom).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 6.2 uses 'evidence of insurability satisfactory to us', so the omission of the qualifier here is a small inconsistency in phrasing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite quantum — premium sufficient for the next two Monthly Insurance Charges; the cross-reference to 'Section 5.2' should be 5.3.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.2 is the interest rate provision and 5.3 is the Monthly Insurance Charge, so the citation misdirects, though harmlessly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any Policy Indebtedness which existed at the end of the Grace Period will be reinstated, if it is not paid' is terse but its operation is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.4's treatment of indebtedness and with 3.4(4)'s freeze of values as at lapse.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Freezing account value, indebtedness and surrender charges 'as in effect when the Policy lapsed' is a definite rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses 'Surrender Charges' where Section 1 and 5.6 speak of a 'Surrender Fee' — a terminology mismatch across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Truncated to 'the effective date of the reinstatement will be the Mont...'; as printed it states no rule at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The missing date interacts with 7.8's two-year contestability of reinstatements and with the Monthly Due Date convention.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short bar on reinstatement after the policy 'has been returned for its Surrender Value'; unambiguous in substance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.8 (surrender terminates all insurance) and with 3.4's opening words.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear allocation: Surrender Value to the Owner if the Insured lives, Death Proceeds to the Beneficiary if not, on proof of death and return of the policy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits 2.5, 5.7 and 8.4; the only strain is that it speaks of paying Surrender Value while the Insured is living without conditioning on a surrender request, which 5.8 supplies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line spendthrift statement expressly qualified 'to the extent permitted by law'; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the policy addresses creditor claims; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An OCR-shredded heading sentence saying only that the amount depends on the Specified Amount and Coverage Option in effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The substance is supplied by the Option A and Option B paragraphs that follow, and by Section 1's 'OPTION A' designation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise two-limb greater-of formula, but limb 1 adds 'any premiums received since the prior Monthly Due Date along with interest', which is unusual and open to argument about which premiums count.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the closing paragraph of 4.2, which separately adds 'any premiums received after the date of death' — an overlap that could double count.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Parallel greater-of formula for Option B; definite arithmetic, with a typographical 'prior to our coinciding with' that does not change meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the 2.14 definition of Option B and with 5.9's statement that Option B leaves the Specified Amount unchanged.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Increased ... by any premiums received after the date of death' is an odd and arguably erroneous adjustment, and 'any indebtedness under the Policy' is broader than the defined 'Policy Indebtedness'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with Option A limb 1 (premiums since the prior Monthly Due Date) and with 9.4 (indebtedness deducted from Proceeds), so the same items are dealt with twice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A unilateral power to 'modify the death benefits' coupled with the Owner's right to refuse leaves the consequence of refusal wholly unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against 6.4 (changes must be approved and signed by an officer and endorsed on the policy) and 7.1 (entire contract), which say how the contract may be altered.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Interest 'at an annual rate determined by us but never less than the rate required by the state in which the Insured resides' fixes only a floor and leaves the rate to the insurer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision sets a death-proceeds interest rate; Option 5's 4% floor applies to left-on-deposit sums, a different situation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The core valuation formula 'A + B + C - D - E' has lost most of its component definitions in the text as printed, and what survives mis-cites the Monthly Insurance Charge to 'Section 2'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Policy Account Value drives 5.6, 5.7, 5.10, 9.4 and both death benefit options, so an incomplete formula ripples through the whole instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The worked example is arithmetically wrong on its face — '6% less 2 points equals 6%' — a mechanical error in the very illustration of the loan-rate offset.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on a Policy Loan Interest Rate 'specified in Section 1', a page that is illegible, and interacts with 9.3's charging rate; the crediting/charging spread is thus stated inconsistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States the monthly charge equals cost of insurance plus rider costs; simple and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches 2.15 in substance, although 2.15 cross-refers to 4.3 rather than to this section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Cost of Insurance on any Premium Due Date' uses a term the policy never defines (the defined term is Monthly Due Date), rates are stated 'per $1,050' rather than $1,000, and 'our expectation of future experience' is open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The mismatch with 2.17's Monthly Due Date and with 5.3's monthly deduction cycle is a real internal inconsistency about when the charge is computed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two-limb adjustment for special risk classes is so garbled that neither the percentage nor the flat-extra method can be applied as printed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1 designates the risk class as 'STANDARD', so the special-class adjustment may never bite on this policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference to Section 1 for rider costs; nothing to construe here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1 does list a 'Waiver of Deduction Rider', so the reference has a referent, albeit a barely legible one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The formula's operator is missing and component 'C' — a clawback of interest credited above the guaranteed rate in the preceding 12 months — is an unusual deduction whose reach is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cash Value feeds 5.7 Surrender Value and 9.4's lapse test, so an indeterminate 'C' unsettles the lapse and surrender machinery.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two-line subtraction: Cash Value less Policy Indebtedness; as clean as any provision in the policy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.4 and 5.10, which express the lapse test in the equivalent terms of Cash Value less indebtedness.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Grant of a surrender right 'at any time' with a deferral power of up to six months 'unless the surrender is used to pay premiums on another Policy with us'; the deferral trigger is unqualified but plainly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with 5.7 (Surrender Value) and 3.4 (no reinstatement after surrender), and I found no clause contradicting the deferral.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The withdrawal cap ('no more than the Surrender Value less $25 and less the next Monthly Insurance Charges'), the charge formula 'A + B + $25' with B undefined in the text, and the recomputation of the 'first year Surrender Fee' are all obscure as printed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reduces the Specified Amount under Option A subject to the 'Minimum Specified Amount shown in Section 1' — an illegible figure — and interacts with 5.6, 5.7 and the 5.10 no-lapse test which subtracts Partial Withdrawals.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The lapse trigger sentence has lost its verb ('if the Surrender Value on a Monthly Due Date is not [sufficient to] pay the next Monthly Insurance Charges'), and 'A Grace Period of 60 days will be allowed for payment of additional premium' leaves unclear what amount cures.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states the lapse test by reference to Surrender Value while 9.4 states it as the excess of Cash Value over Policy Indebtedness and imposes lapse 'whenever' that fails, with no grace period mentioned — a real conflict about when and whether the policy lapses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'At least 50 days before the end of the Grace Period' cannot be right within a 60-day grace period that begins only on the failure — a mechanical numeral error (almost certainly 30) that changes the notice obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be reconciled with the 60-day period in 5.10 and with the annual-report lapse warning in 7.4(10), and notice adequacy is exactly what a lapse dispute turns on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'If adequate premium is not paid by the end of the Grace Period, this Policy will terminate without value' turns on the undefined measure of 'adequate premium'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Terminate without value' sits uneasily with 3.4, which allows reinstatement for five years and revives the pre-lapse Policy Account Value, and with 5.7's Surrender Value.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any premium which remains unpaid on the date of death' presupposes a premium being due, a concept alien to a flexible-premium policy where no premium is ever strictly owed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pulls against 3.2's freedom to pay 'at any time and in any amount' and against 5.10's charge-based lapse test, leaving the deductible amount indeterminate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional no-lapse guarantee with a pro-rata formula; the arithmetic is spelled out even though the OCR clips the final words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the lapse rule in the same section and duplicates the test in 3.2(2), but 9.4's unqualified 'your Policy will lapse whenever' makes no allowance for it — a genuine harmonisation problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard valuation-basis language naming the 1958 CSO table and 4.5% reserve interest; technical but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.6's floor of 'the minimum Cash Value required by the state in which this Policy is delivered'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short procedural right to request changes in writing; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It governs 6.2 and 6.3 and is qualified by 6.4's officer-approval requirement; the fit is orderly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare heading sentence subjecting Specified Amount changes to conditions set out below.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The conditions do follow immediately, and 2.12 anticipates them; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four enumerated, checkable conditions for an increase; 'satisfactory to us' is discretionary but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Condition 4 depends on a 'Minimum Increase in Specified Amount' figure in Section 1 that is illegible, and 7.8 separately restarts contestability for increases.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is scrambled ('effective on the Monthly Due Date following our approval ... shown on an addition to Section 1'), leaving the effective-date rule readable only by reconstruction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It ties to 2.7's Effective Date definition, which points to 6.2 for increases, so the two must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A permissive cap of one increase per 12 months; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallels 3.2(4)'s power to limit additional premiums in any 12-month period; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reverse-order allocation rule is clear, but the closing sentence about the amount 'remaining in force after any requested decrease' is cut off mid-clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.9 imposes an analogous Minimum Specified Amount floor on withdrawals; the truncated floor here should mirror it but does not say so.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: As printed it addresses only a change from Option A to Option B and defines the new Specified Amount as 'the death benefit less' something illegible; the omission of any A-from-B route invites an expressio unius reading.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2.14 and 4.2 treat the two options symmetrically, so a one-way change right is hard to reconcile with the rest of the death-benefit scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any change to your Policy that is not provided for in this section must be approved by us and signed by our President, Vice President, or Secretary', plus a flat denial of agent authority; broad but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinforces 7.1's entire-contract clause but is in tension with 4.1's unilateral power to modify death benefits and with the insurer's unilateral changes under 3.2(3) and 5.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard integration clause; the missing comma after 'This Policy' is cosmetic and the components named are specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the policy plus applications are the entire contract, yet Section 1, riders and the attached Schedule of Benefits (see 5.9) also form part of the deal — a familiar tension worth checking against 6.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Representations-not-warranties language with an 'in the absence of fraud' carve-out; conventional and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works alongside 7.8 incontestability, which is the operative time bar; the two are complementary rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A later-of rule with an embedded proviso about health and insurability 'remaining as stated in the application', and it mis-cites 'Section 7.7 - Incontestability' when incontestability is 7.8 and 7.7 is misstatement of age.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That wrong cross-reference plus 3.1's flat 'no insurance coverage in effect until the payment is made' and 2.7's definition give three different accounts of when cover attaches.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A ten-item disclosure list; item 10's lapse-warning sentence is ungrammatical but the reporting duties themselves are itemised and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The lapse warning must be squared with 5.10(1)'s separate pre-lapse notice and with 9.4, and reporting failures are the sort of thing a lapse claimant reaches for.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fragmentary ('we will send you a [report at any] time during the year for a reasonable charge'); 'reasonable charge as determined by us' is self-judging.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the same right in 7.5 on identical terms, which is redundancy rather than contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An optional projection report for a charge; the projections' basis sentence is cut off but the obligation is minor and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps 7.4's additional-report right without conflicting with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Within two years from the Issue Date' uses 'Issue Date', a term the policy never defines — Section 2 defines Policy Date and Effective Date instead.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 7.8 uses the same undefined 'Issue Date' while 7.2 and 2.6 run periods from the Policy Date, so the two-year clocks in the instrument do not share a defined starting point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Only a shredded remnant of the misstatement-of-age-and-sex adjustment survives, so the adjustment method cannot be applied from the words printed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 7.2 cross-refers to 'Section 7.7 - Incontestability', mislabelling this very provision, which compounds the difficulty of placing it in the scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out 'unless the Surrender Value is insufficient to cover the next Monthly Cost of Insurance' would let the insurer contest a policy at exactly the moment of lapse — an exception that is both unusual and unclear in scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts across 5.10 and 9.4, which treat insufficiency as causing lapse rather than as reopening contestability, and against 3.4's reinstatement right; that is a genuine whole-instrument strain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any Increase in the Specified Amount may not be contested after it has been in effect for two years' is a clean parallel rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It runs alongside the first paragraph of 7.8 and 6.2's increase requirements; no contradiction, though it does not carry the same Surrender Value exception, which is itself notable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence: no share in earnings, no dividends; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the cover page describing the policy as nonparticipating.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'You may exercise every right provided by your Policy if: (1) there is no irrevocable beneficiary; and (2) the Policy has not been assigned' reads as an all-or-nothing suspension of every owner right on either condition, which is almost certainly broader than intended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 8.3 says only that the Owner's and any revocable beneficiary's rights are 'subject to' an assignment, and 8.4 limits only beneficiary changes, so the absolute condition here is hard to reconcile with those narrower provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The change-of-ownership mechanics survive only in fragments (notice, effective date, endorsement), so the operative rule is incomplete on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors 8.4's change-of-beneficiary machinery and is qualified by 8.1; the parallel is coherent as far as it can be read.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Assignment right with a notice condition and a disclaimer of responsibility for validity; standard and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 8.1 makes assignment a bar to exercising 'every right', which is a stronger consequence than 'subject to any assignment' stated here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear default rules: application designation controls, Owner is beneficiary if none named, proceeds paid to the beneficiary except as provided in the section.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1 records 'BENEFICIARY: AS SPECIFIED ON THE [application]' and 2.4 says the same, so the provisions align; the application itself is not in the record.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite survivorship cascade ending with the Owner's executor or administrator; no competing reading.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.1's direction that Death Proceeds go to the Beneficiary and with 2.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Effective upon the date your request was signed but will have no effect on any payment made or other action taken by us before we receive it' is a familiar relation-back rule, definite though it can produce hard facts.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches 8.2's identical formula for ownership changes and is subject to 8.1's irrevocable-beneficiary condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reduced to a stub ('you may obtain a Policy loan ... this Policy assigned to us is the only security needed'), so the loan right's conditions are not visible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is filled out by 9.2-9.4 and by 5.2's loan-rate offset; nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The base figure from which the deductions are taken has dropped out entirely, leaving 'the amount [available is the ...] loan less' two subtractions — unusable as printed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes the Cash Value/Surrender Value definitions in 5.6-5.7 and the charge schedule in 5.3, none of which fixes the missing base.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Interest charged 'at the rate specified in Section [1]' with unpaid interest added to the loan; clear in operation, dependent on an external figure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.2 credits loan-securing account value at that same Section 1 rate less two points, and the illustrative arithmetic there is wrong, so the net loan cost is stated inconsistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines indebtedness and then states an unconditional lapse rule — 'your Policy will lapse whenever' the excess of Cash Value over indebtedness is insufficient — with no grace period or notice built in.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That directly overlaps 5.10, which conditions lapse on a 60-day grace period and prior notice, and takes no account of 5.10's first-two-year no-lapse guarantee; this is the clearest internal conflict in the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is jumbled but identifies the payee and makes the election 'subject to Section 8'; the reference to Section 8 (ownership/beneficiary) rather than to a settlement provision is odd.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with 8.1's condition on exercising rights and with 10.2's basis-of-options rule, which together determine who may actually elect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Lump-sum payment at claim settlement; the simplest provision in the section.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.1 and 4.3's interest-from-death obligation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Either for a specified period or for a specified amount, the present value, which is equal to the Policy Proceeds' is grammatically broken and the 4% floor sits beside an unstated declared rate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Fixed Period table that follows gives specific dollar factors, and 10.2 says amounts will be determined at rates 'in effect at the time of settlement' — the guaranteed table and the current-rate rule need reconciling.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The stated guarantee for a male age 65 is '$6.77 per $1,000' and the alternative figure is printed as '$6,384', an obvious mechanical error in a rate figure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Payments for Life table shows 6.72 for a male age 65 with no certain period, which does not match the $6.77 stated in the text — a direct inconsistency between the narrative option and the table it depends on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Survives only as disconnected phrases about two payees and a guaranteed minimum period, and the guaranteed rates are merely 'furnished upon request'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Unlike Options 2 and 3 it has no table in the instrument, so its guarantees exist only outside the policy — a coherence point against 10.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Badly truncated; the withdrawal right and the limiting proviso ('unless the Beneficiary designation limits withdrawals') are both cut off mid-sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A beneficiary-imposed restriction on withdrawals sits against 8.4, which does not provide for restrictive designations, and against 10.1's election right.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Our rates in effect at the time of settlement' with a present-value equality statement; the rule is short but its interaction with guaranteed minimums is not addressed here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Options 2, 3, 4 and 5 each promise rates 'never less than' a guaranteed floor or table, so this current-rate rule must be read as subject to those floors — a real harmonisation question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single administrative sentence; nothing capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Merely supplements the monthly tables; no conflict anywhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of guarantee periods is corrupted ('not less than %10, Ss, -or 20 years'), so the elective periods cannot be read off the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The table columns show 5, 10, 15 and 20 years certain, which supplies what the sentence garbles, and Option 3's stated 6.77/6.384 figures do not match those columns.
